facts.scope: Host-measured source stroke attributes normalized to a 24-unit grid. Native pixel width is width * nativeSize / 24. Different widths can be optically appropriate; equality or inequality is not a quality verdict. These facts do not establish style calibration or measure expanded filled contours.

meaning.evidence: Inside the ring, two diagonal arms converge into a vertical stem (native.png outlined y6: x6=22 and x9=22 with x7=189/x8=194 between them; y7: x7=x8=17) and that stem is crossed by two horizontal bars at y8 and y10. A Y with a double crossbar is the yen mark; the won alternative would show the three-stroke W seen in reference-4/5.

style.evidence: The ring weight matches the family exactly (2 on the 24 grid, as in references 0/2/4), terminals are flat-cut and the glyph fills the ring to the same clearance seen in reference-2 and reference-4 at 2x. The detail is 1.5 vs the family's 1.8, but in the 2x and enlarged-vector columns the yen bars sit at a weight comparable to the peso crossbars and won strokes, which reads as an optical thinning to hold the stacked-bar gap rather than a weight mismatch.

optics.evidence: At 1x the double-bar counter survives on both surfaces: outlined bars y8/y10 read x6=51 against gap row y9 x6=163, and filled bars read x22=204 against gap x22=102. The one weak feature is the stem tail below the lower bar at y11 (x7/x8=208 outlined, x23/x24=45 filled, ~18% coverage each), a sub-pixel terminal rather than a meaning-bearing counter, and it is solid at 2x.
optics.treatment: None required; optionally snap the sub-bar stem tail to a full pixel row at 16px so it is not left as a haze.

family.evidence: Both paints share the concept, ring diameter and layout: the crossbars land on the same rows y8 and y10 in the outlined cell (x5-x10) and the filled cell (x21-x26), with arms converging at the same y7. The filled version differs only by knocking the glyph out of a solid disc, a deliberate paint inversion rather than a redraw.
